messages.content:
You are the Solution Architect of a legacy modernization platform. From the approved business rules and the
inventory of the legacy (procedures, tables, parameters with neutral types) you design the target service. The
design is hexagonal inside: entities, ports to persistence, and use cases that implement the rules. A person
approves it at gate C3 before any code is generated.

Rules of the design:
- One bounded context (`context`, lowercase) and a Java base package (`base_package`, e.g. com.bank.payments).
- `entities`: the data the use cases work with, usually one per legacy table that holds business data, with
  `table` (target table, snake_case), `legacy_table`, `key` and `fields`. Every field has a neutral type written
  exactly like `decimal(19,4,signed)`, `integer(32,signed)`, `integer(64,signed)`, `text(fixed,3,iso8859-1)`,
  `text(var,40,iso8859-1)`, `timestamp(local)`, `date(yyyy-MM-dd)` or `boolean`. Keep the legacy precision.
- `ports`: interfaces the domain uses to read and write data or to call other systems (e.g. OrderRepository,
  DebitGateway). Each method has `inputs` (with neutral types) and `returns`: an entity name (returned as
  Optional), "boolean", "int", "long" or null for void.
- `use_cases`: each implements a group of rules (`rules` lists their ids; every rule must be in a use case),
  with `inputs`, `outputs`, the business `errors` (a stable `code` like ORDER_NOT_FOUND, the `legacy_code` the old
  system returned and its message), the `ports` it uses, `http_method` and `path`.
- `decisions`: the architecture decisions a reviewer must know (transactions, what stays in the database, what
  changes behaviour on purpose).
- Names are Java identifiers (letters and digits, no reserved words). Infrastructure of the legacy (error-code
  plumbing, logging calls, @@error checks) is not translated: exceptions and the framework replace it.
- Traceability to the legacy, used to replay the golden master on the target: every field has `legacy` (the
  legacy column of an entity field, the legacy parameter of a use case input or output, the argument of the
  external program for a port method input); a port that replaces an external legacy program has
  `legacy_program` and, when a method returns one of its output parameters, `legacy_output`; each use case has
  `legacy_program` and `legacy_message` (the output parameter that carries the message of a rejection);
  `infrastructure` lists the legacy programs that are only infrastructure (e.g. error logging).
- `masks` only for differences with the legacy that are deliberate and explained (`path` like
  `outputs:@o_x`, `when` "always" or "rejected", `reason`). A reviewer approves them at C3 and the verdict lists
  them as not proven; never use them to hide behaviour you did not design.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, with this shape:
{"context": "...", "base_package": "...", "entities": [{"name": "...", "table": "...", "legacy_table": "...",
  "key": ["..."], "fields": [{"name": "...", "type": "...", "column": "...", "legacy": "..."}]}],
 "ports": [{"name": "...", "entity": "...", "legacy_program": null, "methods": [{"name": "...",
  "description": "...", "inputs": [{"name": "...", "type": "...", "legacy": "..."}], "returns": "...",
  "legacy_output": null}]}],
 "use_cases": [{"name": "...", "description": "...", "rules": ["RULE-001"], "inputs": [], "outputs": [],
  "errors": [{"code": "...", "legacy_code": "...", "message": "..."}], "ports": ["..."], "http_method": "POST",
  "path": "/...", "legacy_program": "...", "legacy_message": "..."}],
 "decisions": [{"title": "...", "context": "...", "decision": "...", "consequences": "..."}],
 "infrastructure": ["..."], "masks": []}

It then debits the origin by amount plus commission, credits the destination by the amount, records the transfer with the next number and commits everything in one transaction.","rules":["RULE-001","RULE-002","RULE-003","RULE-005","RULE-006","RULE-007","RULE-008","RULE-009"],"inputs":[{"name":"cuentaOrigen","type":"text(var,10,iso8859-1)","legacy":"txtCuentaOrigen"},{"name":"cuentaDestino","type":"text(var,10,iso8859-1)","legacy":"txtCuentaDestino"},{"name":"monto","type":"decimal(11,2,signed)","legacy":"txtMonto"},{"name":"tipo","type":"text(fixed,3,iso8859-1)","legacy":"ddlTipo"}],"outputs":[{"name":"mensaje","type":"text(var,40,utf8)","legacy":"lblMensaje"},{"name":"comision","type":"text(var,8,utf8)","legacy":"lblComision"},{"name":"numero","type":"integer(32,signed)","legacy":"numero"}],"errors":[{"code":"SAME_ACCOUNT","legacy_code":"-1","message":"LA CUENTA DESTINO ES LA MISMA"},{"code":"ORIGIN_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND","legacy_code":"-1","message":"CUENTA ORIGEN NO EXISTE"},{"code":"ORIGIN_ACCOUNT_INACTIVE","legacy_code":"-1","message":"CUENTA ORIGEN INACTIVA"},{"code":"DESTINATION_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND","legacy_code":"-1","message":"CUENTA DESTINO NO EXISTE"},{"code":"INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE","legacy_code":"-1","message":"SALDO INSUFICIENTE"}],"ports":["CuentaRepository","TransferenciaRepository"],"http_method":"POST","path":"/transferencias","legacy_program":"TRANSFERENCIA","legacy_message":"lblMensaje"},{"name":"ConsultarComprobante","description":"Returns the receipt of a transfer: the requested number as text and the amount stored for it formatted with two decimals ('0.00'). If the transfer does not exist, the amount is an empty string and no error is raised.","rules":["RULE-004"],"inputs":[{"name":"numero","type":"integer(32,signed)","legacy":"numero"}],"outputs":[{"name":"numero","type":"text(var,11,utf8)","legacy":"lblNumero"},{"name":"monto","type":"text(var,12,utf8)","legacy":"lblMonto"}],"errors":[],"ports":["TransferenciaRepository"],"http_method":"GET","path":"/transferencias/{numero}/comprobante","legacy_program":"Comprobante","legacy_message":null}],"decisions":[{"title":"One transaction per transfer","context":"The legacy opens a SqlTransaction, rolls back explicitly on every rejection and commits after the insert.","decision":"RealizarTransferencia runs in a single @Transactional boundary. Business rejections are exceptions that roll the transaction back. The success path commits once, after debit, credit and insert.","consequences":"Same atomicity as the legacy. The explicit Rollback calls and the lblMensaje assignments are replaced by exceptions mapped to HTTP 422 with the stable code and the legacy message text. The rejection checks run before any write."},{"title":"Commission is a pure domain calculation","context":"ComisionService.Calcular is a static helper used only by the transfer page (RULE-001 to RULE-003).","decision":"The calculation becomes a domain component without ports, using BigDecimal. Order: base fee (0.50 if monto <= 1000.00, else monto*0.001 rounded to 2 decimals with RoundingMode.HALF_UP, which is away from zero for the positive amounts here), then cap at 5.00, then +1.00 when tipo equals \"INM\" (case-sensitive). RealizarTransferencia calls it. It has no endpoint of its own.","consequences":"An INM commission can reach 6.00. The calculation is covered by unit tests with the rule scenarios and is replayed through the TRANSFERENCIA traces."},{"title":"Legacy column precision kept","context":"The rules describe money as decimal(19,4), but the legacy tables use DECIMAL(13,2) for balances, DECIMAL(11,2) for amounts and DECIMAL(7,2) for commissions.","decision":"Entities and port inputs use the precision of the legacy columns. The amount input is decimal(11,2), and balance updates are database-side (saldo = saldo +/- valor).","consequences":"No change in stored values. An amount with more than two decimals is rejected at the API boundary (HTTP 400). The legacy would have rounded it silently on insert."},{"title":"Next transfer number kept as MAX+1, with a row lock on the origin","context":"The legacy reads the balance without a lock and computes the number with ISNULL(MAX(TRF_NUMERO),0)+1, which is racy under concurrency.","decision":"The numbering rule is kept (RULE-009) and is read inside the same transaction. The origin account is read with a row lock (findByNumeroForUpdate), so the balance check and the debit are consistent. The primary key still forbids duplicate numbers.","consequences":"Sequential behaviour is identical to the legacy and to the traces. Under concurrency, a primary-key collision or a deadlock victim returns HTTP 409 and the client may retry. This only differs from the legacy in cases where the legacy could produce duplicate-key errors or an overdraft."},{"title":"Page validators move to the API boundary","context":"Transferencia.aspx has validators: origin required and 10 digits, destination required, amount required and between 1 and 10000, and a dropdown that only allows PRO or INM. They are not business rules. int.Parse in Comprobante throws an unhandled error on a bad number.","decision":"Bean Validation on the request reproduces these checks and returns HTTP 400 with no business error code. The type must be PRO or INM. A non-numeric receipt number is also an HTTP 400.","consequences":"Requests that the legacy page would block (or that crashed it) are rejected before the use case. The business rules are unchanged. The traces only contain inputs that pass these validations."},{"title":"Receipt formatting and replay coverage","context":"RULE-004 requires the amount as text with two decimals, blank if the transfer does not exist. There is no trace of the Comprobante page.","decision":"ConsultarComprobante returns numero and monto as text (monto formatted '0.00', empty string when not found) and responds 200 in both cases. The commission of the transfer response is also text formatted '0.00' (lblComision).","consequences":"Text outputs keep trailing zeros, which a JSON number would lose. RULE-004 is verified only by its scenarios, not by golden master replay."},{"title":"Configuration and presentation are replaced","context":"Web.config holds the connection string with integrated security. The .aspx pages, the redirect to Comprobante.aspx and Page_Load only handle UI.","decision":"The datasource is configured through the Spring configuration and secrets of the platform. The POST response returns numero and the client navigates to the receipt. Page_Load, which only clears lblMensaje, is not translated.","consequences":"No UI behaviour is migrated. Legacy-visible outputs are exposed as response fields."}],"infrastructure":["Transferencia.Page_Load"],"masks":[]}
